# Systems General Run Workflow Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `completed`
- Updated: `2026-07-29T03:17:49Z`

## Objective

Replace reference-system-specific Run & Test panels with one configurable, capability-driven workflow that remains safe, extensible, and shared across desktop and thin-client hosts.

## Discovery

Systems Run & Test currently mounts three interaction panels that mirror the three shipped reference-system families, followed by a separate general deployment workflow. The desktop and thin-client pages hard-code those panels, while deployment contracts and runtime adapters also classify releases through a closed SystemReferenceRuntimeKind union. Existing execution-run and runtime-execution contracts provide reusable lifecycle and adapter foundations, but the repository has no application-owned catalog that describes which safe user workflows an exact release supports. A durable design must select workflows from verified release capabilities and host support rather than from reference-template identity or renderer branching.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: A general Run & Test workflow crosses exact-release integrity, workspace isolation, authorization, deployment, data/artifact access, controlled invocation, runtime capability, and diagnostic boundaries. Extensibility must not turn release metadata or renderer configuration into authority or a dynamic-code execution path.
- Protected assets:
  - Exact approved release, reviewed execution plan, and implementation identities
  - Workspace and organization isolation
  - Conversation approval and runtime invocation authority
  - System-data mutation and artifact-review authorization
  - Deployment, secret-reference, egress, quota, and bounded-run policy
  - Execution history, audit evidence, diagnostics, and private runtime content
- Trust boundaries:
  - Release and workflow discovery to application-owned profile resolution
  - Shared renderer workflow selection to desktop IPC or authenticated thin-client transport
  - Declarative input values to application validation and an allowlisted handler
  - Application orchestration to host-composed runtime, data, artifact, and deployment adapters
  - Runtime/provider results to bounded sanitized result projections
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - A forged workflow or handler id invokes an operation not supported by the exact release or host
  - Release metadata supplies executable code, arbitrary routes, raw component names, or policy that the renderer trusts
  - A stale profile is executed against another release, plan, workspace, or deployment
  - Selecting or opening a workflow silently approves, installs, mutates, or starts work
  - A generic input envelope bypasses field bounds, capability policy, egress, secret, quota, or authorization checks
  - Unknown result content exposes provider payloads, secrets, paths, private messages, or unbounded collections
  - Host-specific registration creates parity gaps or bypasses the shared application use case
- Controls:
  - Application-owned catalog derives bounded profiles from exact verified release/plan evidence plus host-supported handler registrations
  - Closed versioned input and result primitive kinds are normalized and bounded; unknown kinds fail closed
  - Profile selection is read-only and every state-changing action remains an explicit existing or new application command
  - Handlers delegate to existing domain-specific use cases and preserve their authorization, integrity, approval, readiness, sandbox, policy, quota, audit, and workspace checks
  - Execution records retain exact source context and handler/profile identity without persisting private raw payloads
  - Transports expose allowlisted DTOs and safe diagnostics only; hosts compose registrations but do not branch on reference templates
  - Lazy loading and collection limits prevent unselected workflows and unbounded results from consuming protected resources
- Verification:
  - Contract normalization and rejection tests for unknown, oversized, duplicate, stale, and cross-workspace profile/input/result identities
  - Application catalog and handler tests proving exact release/plan binding, host capability intersection, no mutation during discovery, and fail-closed dispatch
  - Regression tests for existing conversation approval, data authorization, review redaction, deployment policy, audit, and cancellation paths through the general boundary
  - Desktop IPC, API, preload, and thin-client parity tests that reject renderer-supplied authority fields and unsupported handlers
  - Shared UI interaction tests for discovery, configuration, review, explicit execution, bounded results/history, lazy loading, keyboard use, loading, empty, blocked, and failure states
  - Architecture, documentation, agent-support, server/thin-client build, security-focused, and repository completion gates
- Residual risks:
  - A finite workflow primitive set cannot represent every future interaction; new primitive families require an explicit reviewed extension.
  - Imported or authored executable workflows remain unavailable until a qualified sandbox and controlled-environment evidence exist.
  - Automated UI and host checks do not replace physical assistive-technology, production capacity, or managed-environment qualification.

### Constraints

- Replace reference-template and reference-runtime-kind branching with verified capability/profile resolution; adding another reference system that reuses supported capabilities must not require another Run & Test panel.
- Use one shared workflow shell and shared bounded interaction primitives for desktop and thin client; host code composes clients and supported handlers without owning product behavior.
- Keep design-time asset configuration schemas separate from runtime workflow input contracts and never treat renderer state or inert asset metadata as execution authority.
- Resolve every workflow against an exact workspace-owned approved release or reviewed execution plan and an application/host-supported handler before presenting it as runnable.
- Workflow discovery and selection are read-only. Approval, deployment, mutation, invocation, retry, and cancellation remain explicit application commands with their existing authorization and integrity checks.
- Preserve separate conversation, system-data, system-review, deployment, and execution record families behind the general workflow boundary rather than coercing their persistence models into one record.
- Imported or authored executable content remains unavailable without an independently qualified sandbox and explicit host support; unknown profile, handler, capability, schema, or result kinds fail closed.
- Lazy-load only the selected workflow and bound input, output, history, diagnostics, and rendered collections.
- Implement this successor in economically meaningful increments and run the full suite only after each complete increment, using focused tests for internal chunks.

## High-level decisions

### General Run & Test workflow authority

Where should configurable Run & Test workflow definitions and dispatch authority live?

The user experience should be one configurable workflow rather than one panel per reference system. The selected boundary must let future reference systems reuse supported interactions without adding renderer branches, while keeping exact-release verification, authorization, policy, runtime support, and execution side effects outside untrusted metadata and UI state.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `application-owned-capability-profiles`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Application-owned capability profiles (application-owned-capability-profiles) | Add a versioned application-owned workflow catalog that resolves an exact approved release or reviewed plan into supported profiles. One shared UI shell renders a fixed set of bounded reusable interaction primitives—such as form, table, transcript, artifact preview, status, confirmation, and history—and dispatches explicit actions through allowlisted application handlers composed by each host. Existing conversation, data, review, deployment, and execution use cases remain authoritative behind those handlers. | yes | Requires new contracts, application catalog/handler ports, transport parity, and migration of the current panels into reusable primitives.; Avoids a universal runtime payload while removing reference-template UI branching.; Future reference systems that compose existing capabilities require profile registration/configuration but no new Systems page or panel.; A genuinely new interaction primitive still requires a reviewed contract and renderer extension. | Run & Test becomes one select-configure-review-run-results experience driven by verified capabilities.; Workflow descriptors remain inert presentation and validation data; handlers and policy stay application/host owned.; The closed deployment referenceRuntimeKind seam can be replaced by stable handler/profile identities without weakening exact release checks.; Desktop and thin client share behavior and lazy-load only the selected workflow. |
| Release-declared workflow language (release-declared-workflow-dsl) | Compile complete declarative workflow definitions into each release and let a generic interpreter render and execute their typed steps through a capability broker. | no | Provides the greatest portability and could eventually support authored workflows.; Requires a new signed workflow language, compiler, interpreter, policy proof, migration/versioning model, sandbox qualification, and substantially broader threat analysis.; Makes release artifacts a larger security-sensitive public contract. | Reference and future authored systems could define novel workflows without application registration.; The current repository does not yet have the sandbox and controlled-environment evidence required for that broader execution authority.; Delivery risk and security scope are materially larger than the requested replacement. |

## Increment 1: Capability-driven workflow core and host boundary

- Id: `general-workflow-core`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: None

Provide one versioned, bounded application contract that discovers and dispatches supported workflows for an exact approved release or reviewed execution plan without reference-template branching or renderer-owned authority.

### Work packages

- **Workflow profile contracts and bounds** (`workflow-contracts`): A system-run-workflow contract family defines stable profile/source/action identities, closed reusable input and result primitive kinds, explicit confirmation semantics, safe diagnostics, collection and payload limits, normalization, and fail-closed versioning without executable metadata.
- **Application catalog and allowlisted dispatch** (`application-catalog-dispatch`): Application use cases derive profiles from an exact workspace-owned approved release or reviewed plan plus host-supported registrations, prepare bounded snapshots, validate actions, and delegate explicit commands to existing conversation, system-data, system-review, deployment, and execution services.
- **Reusable handlers for current supported capabilities** (`current-capability-handlers`): The controlled conversation, release-bound data, release-bound review, and deploy/run capabilities register as reusable workflow profiles rather than reference-system UI types, while their distinct record, authorization, approval, integrity, policy, audit, and cancellation semantics remain authoritative.
- **Host composition and transport parity** (`transport-host-migration`): Desktop and server hosts compose the same application catalog and supported handlers; API, IPC, preload, and client contracts expose only generic profile discovery, snapshot, and explicit-action operations with allowlisted request fields and safe result projections.
- **Stable runtime profile identity** (`deployment-profile-migration`): The closed SystemReferenceRuntimeKind deployment seam is replaced by stable runtime profile/handler identity, with bounded compatibility handling for existing persisted trusted-reference deployments and fail-closed rejection of unknown or unsupported mappings.
- **Architecture, security, and operational documentation** (`core-security-docs`): Canonical decisions and architecture explain the application-owned profile boundary, exact-source requirements, finite primitives, host responsibility, migration behavior, rollback, unsupported authored execution, and controlled-environment limits.

### Deliverables

- System run workflow contracts, normalization, limits, and tests
- Application workflow catalog, handler registry ports, orchestration use cases, and denial tests
- Capability handlers covering the current conversation, data, review, and deployment behaviors
- Desktop/server host composition and generic API/IPC/preload/client parity
- Deployment runtime-profile persistence compatibility and migration tests
- Updated ADRs, architecture documentation, context packs, README guidance, and security review

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exact-source-profile-resolution`: Workflow discovery returns only profiles supported by the exact workspace-owned approved release or reviewed execution plan and the current host; stale, unknown, unsupported, cross-workspace, and integrity-invalid sources fail closed. | local | passed (test) |
| `read-only-discovery`: Listing, selecting, or preparing a profile performs no approval, deployment, mutation, invocation, retry, cancellation, provider call, or runtime execution. | local | passed (test) |
| `bounded-generic-contract`: The generic boundary accepts only versioned closed primitive kinds and bounded values, rejects executable metadata and unsupported authority fields, and returns sanitized bounded results and diagnostics. | local | passed (test) |
| `existing-capability-parity`: Controlled conversation, release-bound data, release-bound review, and deploy/run operations are reachable through registered generic profiles while retaining their existing exact identity, authorization, approval, integrity, policy, audit, quota, cancellation, and record-family behavior. | local | passed (test) |
| `transport-and-host-parity`: Desktop IPC/preload and authenticated server API expose equivalent generic workflow behavior, and hosts register supported handlers without branching on reference template ids. | local | passed (test) |
| `deployment-profile-compatibility`: Existing trusted-reference deployment records remain readable through an explicit compatibility mapping, new records use stable runtime profile identity, and unknown or ambiguous mappings are rejected without activation or execution. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-core-impact-reviewed`: Threats, controls, denial paths, safe diagnostics, persistence migration, rollback, unsupported sandbox scope, and residual risk are documented and evidenced. | local | passed (review) |

### Verification

- Run focused contract normalization and size/version rejection tests while implementing the contract package.
- Run focused application catalog/handler tests for exact-source resolution, no-side-effect discovery, unsupported handler, stale source, cross-workspace, authorization denial, and sanitized failure behavior.
- Run existing conversation, system-data, system-review, system-deployment, execution-run, persistence, and runtime adapter tests through the registered handlers.
- Run API/IPC/preload/host parity tests, including rejection of renderer-supplied policy, handler, capability, runtime, workspace, and authority fields.
- Run deployment persistence compatibility tests for legacy trusted-reference records, new runtime-profile records, unknown mappings, and restart-safe reads.
- After all work packages are complete, run npm run docs:check, npm run architecture:check, npm run agent-support:check, applicable security-focused tests, npm run build:server, npm run build:thin-client, and npm test once for the increment.

### Rollback

Keep the existing feature-specific transports and UI consumers operational while the generic core is additive. If the increment fails qualification, remove the unconsumed generic transport/catalog registrations and restore the prior deployment field writer while retaining a read-only compatibility test; do not rewrite or delete persisted deployment or execution evidence.

### Excluded

- Run & Test page cutover or deletion of the existing shared panels, which belongs to Increment 2
- A release-authored workflow language or generic dynamic-code interpreter
- Imported or authored executable workflows without a qualified sandbox
- New provider, tool, retrieval, multimodal, image-generation, or arbitrary workflow runtime capabilities
- Production or managed-environment capacity qualification

## Increment 2: General configurable Run & Test experience

- Id: `general-run-test-experience`
- Status: `completed`
- Dependencies: `general-workflow-core`

Replace the reference-system-specific and deployment panel stack with one shared, accessible, lazy configurable workflow that guides users through source selection, workflow selection, configuration, review, explicit action, results, and history.

### Work packages

- **Shared workflow shell** (`shared-workflow-shell`): A single desktop/thin-client component presents release or reviewed-plan selection, supported workflow selection, purpose and prerequisites, bounded configuration, a review step, an explicit action, results, history, and a clear way to change workflows.
- **Reusable interaction and result primitives** (`bounded-ui-primitives`): Accessible reusable form, table, transcript, artifact-preview, status, confirmation, audit/history, loading, empty, blocked, and failure primitives render only application-projected descriptors and results.
- **Lazy loading and bounded state** (`lazy-state-and-performance`): The page loads profile summaries first and requests snapshot, detail, history, or result data only for the selected workflow; workspace/source changes cancel or discard stale responses and clear private state.
- **Desktop and thin-client cutover** (`host-page-cutover`): Both Systems pages use the same generic client/component boundary; reference-specific Run & Test wrappers and mounted shared panels are removed, and deployment is available through the same workflow shell without weakening its operational lifecycle.
- **End-to-end qualification and user documentation** (`experience-qualification-docs`): Interaction, accessibility, parity, denial, regression, build, and documentation evidence demonstrate a comprehensible general workflow and document how future capability profiles extend it safely.

### Deliverables

- Shared generic Run & Test workflow component and bounded primitive library
- One generic desktop client and one generic thin-client client using the shared contract
- Desktop and thin-client Systems page cutover
- Removal of reference-system-specific Run & Test UI panels, wrappers, and obsolete tests
- Interaction, accessibility, lazy-loading, stale-response, failure, parity, and regression tests
- Updated user, architecture, extension, security, and testing documentation

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `single-general-experience`: Run & Test shows one configurable workflow experience and no longer mounts or labels separate conversation, data-entry, review, or deployment panels by reference-system family. | local | passed (test) |
| `profile-driven-extensibility`: A test fixture can register another release profile using existing primitives and make it available without editing either Systems page or adding a reference-specific React component. | local | passed (test) |
| `current-user-behavior-preserved`: Users can perform the currently supported controlled conversation, data, review, installation, activation, health, bounded run, cancellation, rollback, revocation, result, and audit/history tasks through the general workflow when eligible. | local | passed (test) |
| `explicit-side-effects`: Opening, selecting, configuring, or reviewing a workflow performs no mutation or execution; every state-changing action has a clear label, truthful prerequisites, required confirmation or approval, busy state, result, and recoverable failure state. | local | passed (test) |
| `lazy-bounded-ui`: Unselected workflows issue no detail or protected-data reads, only the selected workflow state is retained, collections and text are bounded, stale workspace/source responses are ignored, and private results are cleared when context changes. | local | passed (test) |
| `accessible-shared-host-parity`: Desktop and thin client share the same keyboard-accessible workflow semantics, focus progression, labels, loading, empty, blocked, confirmation, error, result, and history behavior while using their respective generic clients. | local | passed (test) |
| `security-experience-regression`: UI and host tests prove profile selection cannot grant authority, unsupported actions cannot be forged, diagnostics remain sanitized, and existing authorization, integrity, workspace-isolation, policy, approval, and audit denials remain visible and effective. | local | passed (test) |
| `experience-repository-gates`: Focused UI/client/parity tests pass, followed only after the complete increment by applicable documentation, architecture, agent-support, build, security, visual qualification where available, and repository test gates. | local | passed (test) |

### Verification

- Run focused shared component tests for profile discovery, configuration controls, review/confirmation, explicit actions, result primitives, history, focus/keyboard behavior, loading, empty, blocked, and sanitized failure states.
- Run lazy-loading and stale-context tests proving unselected profiles do not read detail/protected data and workspace/source changes clear or ignore prior state.
- Run fixture extensibility tests proving a new profile using existing primitives requires no Systems page or reference-specific component change.
- Run desktop/thin-client client and page parity tests plus packaged desktop/thin-client visual workflow qualification when the existing harness supports the surface.
- Run the existing conversation, data, review, deployment, execution, authorization, isolation, redaction, policy, audit, and cancellation regression suites through the generic UI/client path.
- After all work packages are complete, run npm run docs:check, npm run architecture:check, npm run agent-support:check, applicable security-focused tests, npm run build:server, npm run build:thin-client, and npm test once for the increment.

### Rollback

Revert both host pages to the prior shared panel stack as one atomic UI rollback while leaving the qualified generic application/transport boundary additive and unused. Do not delete workflow, deployment, execution, audit, data, review, or conversation records.

### Excluded

- A free-form workflow designer or user-authored executable workflow language
- Arbitrary HTML, JavaScript, component imports, routes, handlers, or provider payload rendering
- New runtime capability families beyond those already implemented and registered in Increment 1
- Automatic approval, deployment, execution, retry, cancellation, rollback, or revocation
- Physical assistive-technology, production capacity, or managed-environment qualification not available locally
